Stoutness goes further than plumpness — a solid, settled heaviness — but still stops short of corpulence, which names outright extreme fatness.

Obesity is the clinical term a doctor writes in a chart — neutral, medical, tied to measurements. Corpulence means the same extreme fatness but lives in books rather than clinics: a formal, faintly antique word a novelist or historian reaches for, judgment softened by dignity.
